detections.description: An account other than root has user id 0 and therefore the same privileges as root.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence high: The uid comes directly from /etc/passwd; the only uncertainty is intent, not the observation.
explanation.disclaimer: This is a suspicious indicator. Benign activity can produce the same observation; it does not prove compromise.
missing_corroboration: Account creation time and who created it (auth log, /var/log/wtmp, file times of the home directory).
A shell history or SSH key for the account that nobody recognises.
possible_benign_causes: Some appliance images or migration leftovers deliberately keep a second uid-0 account (for example 'toor').
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity high is the rule's base severity: UID 0 grants full control of the host, but the data alone does not show who created the account or why. The number of matching items did not change it.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-LNX-ACC-001 requires: acct. Satisfied clauses: acct (1 item(s)). Each matching item is reported separately (grouped by key = 'user:toor').
explanation.why_flagged: Linux treats every account with uid 0 as root. Attackers add such an account (often named like a system account) to keep root access that survives a password change of root itself.

investigation_steps: Compare the account against the host's documented account list.
Check /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow modification times and the home directory contents.
Look for logins by this account in wtmp/auth logs and for SSH keys in its home.

matched_conditions.description: A user record other than root has uid 0

attack.explanation: A second uid-0 local account is one way to persist with root access; the data does not show it was created by an adversary.
Such an account could be used as a valid local account for later access.

detections.remediation: If unauthorised, lock the account (usermod -L) after preserving evidence, then remove it and rotate credentials of accounts it could have reached; if legitimate, document it and give it a distinct non-zero uid where possible.
detections.title: Account user:toor has UID 0

detections.description: A system log file is a symbolic link to /dev/null or another device, which silently discards log records.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence high: A link from a log path to a device is an unambiguous configuration fact.
explanation.disclaimer: This is a suspicious indicator. Benign activity can produce the same observation; it does not prove compromise.
possible_benign_causes: Deliberately disabling noisy logs on a diskless or embedded image (rare for auth logs).
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity high is the rule's base severity: Discarded logs remove the evidence defenders depend on, and the configuration has no common benign purpose. The number of matching items did not change it.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-LNX-LOG-001 requires: log. Satisfied clauses: log (1 item(s)).
explanation.why_flagged: Linking /var/log files to /dev/null is a known way to stop recording activity without stopping the logging service.

investigation_steps: Record the link, its target and timestamps (stat), then check who changed it (auth logs from before the change, shell history).
Look for other defense-evasion signs: cleared history files, stopped auditd, altered rsyslog configuration.

attack.explanation: Discarding log output is a form of blocking indicators; the data does not show who did it.
Related to clearing Linux system logs; no clearing is observed, only the redirect.

detections.remediation: Replace the link with a regular file with correct ownership and mode, restart the logging service, and forward logs off the host.

rule.name: System log redirected to a device

detections.title: System log redirected to a device

detections.description: A cron job, systemd unit, startup script or shell profile was flagged for reverse-shell, download-and-execute or world-writable-path behaviour.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence high: A /dev/tcp or netcat reverse-shell pattern has few benign explanations.
explanation.disclaimer: This is a suspicious indicator. Benign activity can produce the same observation; it does not prove compromise.
missing_corroboration: The file's owner, creation time and package ownership.
Outbound connections to the address named in the command.
possible_benign_causes: Backup or monitoring scripts that use /tmp or /dev/tcp for legitimate reasons.
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity high is the rule's base severity: The collector matched command-content patterns that are rarely written by administrators. The number of matching items did not change it.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-LNX-PER-001 requires: entry. Satisfied clauses: entry (1 item(s)), reverse (1 item(s)). The contributing items were grouped because they share id = 'BOF-8e852976a016a806'.
explanation.why_flagged: Jobs and units that open network shells, fetch and run code, or execute from world-writable directories are common footholds that survive reboots.

investigation_steps: Read the full file and identify who last modified it (stat, package verification).
Check for the destination host/port in network logs and current connections.
Look for sibling persistence (other cron.d entries, units, profile scripts).

matched_conditions.description: A persistence finding for suspicious commands

attack.explanation: Cron is a common way to schedule attacker commands; the finding concerns a cron entry only if the check id is PER-CRON-002.
A suspicious systemd unit would be a systemd service persistence candidate.

detections.remediation: Preserve the file as evidence, disable it (do not delete first), and review the accounts and files it touches; restore from a known-good package or backup.
detections.title: Suspicious persistence entry: Synthetic finding PER-CRON-002

detections.description: A service, task, autorun, cron job or unit refers to a path that a filesystem finding (world-writable, temporary, unsigned, hidden or recently modified executable) also lists.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence medium: Linking is by a shared path string in two independent findings; the path is exact but the file's purpose is still unknown.
explanation.disclaimer: These independent indicators were correlated by a rule. Correlation raises a question; it does not prove malicious activity.
missing_corroboration: Hash and signature of the file; creation time relative to the startup entry.
Network connections made by the process started from this path.
possible_benign_causes: Software legitimately installed under ProgramData or /opt that is also unsigned or recently updated.
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity high is the rule's base severity: A startup mechanism that points at a file sitting in an unsafe place or flagged as unusual is the shape of a planted foothold. The number of matching items did not change it.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-ANY-COR-001 requires: (start all file). Satisfied clauses: start (1 item(s)), file (1 item(s)). The contributing items were grouped because they share evidence.paths = '/tmp/.hidden/agent'.
explanation.why_flagged: Two independent collectors (startup configuration and file inspection) describe the same path. That agreement is stronger than either finding alone and shows where to look first.

investigation_steps: Open the shared path: owner, hash, signature, timestamps.
Read the startup entry that references it.
Check whether other entries reference the same path.

matched_conditions.description: A suspicious service, task, autorun or cron/unit finding
A filesystem finding about an unusual executable or writable file

attack.explanation: Service/unit persistence can launch attacker-placed files; here the link is only a shared path.
Scheduled execution can launch attacker-placed files; here the link is only a shared path.

detections.remediation: Preserve the file and the entry as evidence, disable the startup entry, then remove or restore the file from a trusted source.

detections.description: A log-impairment or protection-disabling finding appears on the same host as a high-signal persistence finding.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence medium: Both are accurate findings; their link is that they co-occur, not that one caused the other.
explanation.disclaimer: These independent indicators were correlated by a rule. Correlation raises a question; it does not prove malicious activity.
missing_corroboration: Timestamps showing the persistence artefact was created after logging was reduced.
possible_benign_causes: Hosts with custom logging pipelines that look impaired to the collector, plus an unrelated admin script flagged as persistence.
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity high is the rule's base severity: Persistence indicators are concerning on their own; paired with reduced logging or protection they suggest the host was prepared to avoid detection. The number of matching items did not change it.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-ANY-COR-005 requires: (impair all persist). Satisfied clauses: impair (1 item(s)), persist (2 item(s)).
explanation.why_flagged: Attackers who establish persistence commonly also reduce what is recorded. Co-occurrence prioritises this host for investigation over hosts with only one of the signals.

investigation_steps: Establish the timeline from file and configuration timestamps.
Check whether other hosts show the same pair.
Collect volatile evidence (processes, connections) before changing anything.

attack.explanation: Impairing defences is a tactic used alongside persistence; co-occurrence here does not prove it.

detections.remediation: Restore logging and protection, preserve and then remove the persistence artefact, and review the host for further changes.

detections.description: A telnet, FTP, TFTP or r-service port is listening on an address other than loopback.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence medium: The port number identifies the usual service; the process may be something else, and reachability depends on filtering.
explanation.disclaimer: This is a suspicious indicator. Benign activity can produce the same observation; it does not prove compromise.
missing_corroboration: The listening process name matching the protocol.
Firewall rules allowing the port from untrusted networks.
possible_benign_causes: Legacy device management on an isolated network.
A different service that happens to use one of these ports.
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity high is the rule's base severity: These protocols send credentials or data unprotected, and TFTP has no authentication at all. The number of matching items did not change it.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-ANY-NET-001 requires: lst. Satisfied clauses: lst (1 item(s)). Each matching item is reported separately (grouped by key = 'listener:tcp/0.0.0.0/23').
explanation.why_flagged: Cleartext remote-access protocols expose credentials to anyone on the path and are frequent entry points; a listener on a routable address makes them reachable.

investigation_steps: Identify the owning process and package.
Check firewall policy for the port.
Review authentication logs for the service.

matched_conditions.description: A cleartext-protocol port bound to a non-loopback address

attack.explanation: An exposed remote-access service can serve as an external access point; exposure to attackers is not established.

detections.remediation: Replace with SSH/SFTP (or restrict to a management network) and disable the service once confirmed unnecessary.

detections.description: An unexpected or over-privileged account configuration was found on a host that also has weak authentication controls.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence medium: Both sides are exact findings; their relationship (same accounts, reachable service) is not established by the data.
explanation.disclaimer: These independent indicators were correlated by a rule. Correlation raises a question; it does not prove malicious activity.
missing_corroboration: Evidence that the weak control applies to the privileged account (for example sshd allowing that account).
Logons by the privileged account from unusual sources.
possible_benign_causes: Competition or lab hosts configured deliberately weak.
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity high was set by an explicit rule condition: An authentication-bypass-class weakness (PAM accepts without credential, passwordless accounts, no NLA, auto-logon) is present.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-ANY-PRIV-002 requires: (priv all auth). Satisfied clauses: priv (1 item(s)), auth (2 item(s)), bypass (1 item(s)).
explanation.why_flagged: An attacker needs a way to authenticate and a privileged identity to use. Seeing a questionable privileged account and weak authentication on one host is more actionable than either alone.

investigation_steps: Check whether the privileged account can use the weak authentication path (sshd AllowUsers, PAM stack for the service).
Review authentication logs for the privileged accounts.
Fix the bypass-class weakness first.

attack.explanation: Valid accounts are often used with weak authentication to gain access; nothing here shows use.
Account manipulation is one way a privileged anomaly arises.

detections.remediation: Remove or justify the anomalous privileged account, then close the authentication weakness (PAM/sshd/NLA/lockout) in the order of the severity rationale.

detections.description: A legacy service known for cleartext authentication (telnet, r-services, tftp, FTP) is enabled and a matching process is listening.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence medium: Names identify the service; they do not prove it is reachable from untrusted networks.
explanation.disclaimer: These independent indicators were correlated by a rule. Correlation raises a question; it does not prove malicious activity.
missing_corroboration: Firewall rules showing the port reachable from outside the management network.
possible_benign_causes: Isolated management networks or labs that depend on tftp/ftp for provisioning.
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity high is the rule's base severity: Credentials sent in cleartext and unauthenticated file transfer are directly exploitable on a reachable network. The number of matching items did not change it.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-LNX-SVC-001 requires: (unit all port). Satisfied clauses: unit (1 item(s)), port (1 item(s)).
explanation.why_flagged: An enabled unit says the service starts at boot; a listening process says it is running now. Together they show an exposed cleartext service rather than a stray package.

investigation_steps: Confirm the service owner and whether the port is scored.
Check the firewall policy for the listening port.
Review authentication logs for the service.
